title: LARP: Language Audio Relational Pre-training for Cold-Start Playlist Continuation

problem.claim: Playlist continuation must recommend songs that extend a playlist in a personalized and musically cohesive manner, including when songs lack interaction data.

gap.claim: Existing approaches use frozen pre-trained content models that may not align with a specific musical setting, while current content modules may be incompatible with cold-start recommendation or unable to integrate cross-modal and relational signals effectively.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces LARP, a multimodal cold-start playlist continuation model.
LARP uses a three-stage contrastive learning framework integrating multimodal and relational signals through within-track language-audio, track-track, and track-playlist contrastive losses.
The authors report releasing the code and dataset.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on two publicly available datasets demonstrate LARP's efficacy over unimodal and multimodal models for cold-start playlist continuation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Playlist continuation is important for music streaming services as playlist-based listening grows.
Collaborative-filtering approaches struggle with songs lacking interaction data, creating a cold-start problem.
Existing solutions do not adequately learn setting-aligned content representations or combine cross-modal and relational signals in the cold-start setting.
LARP addresses these limitations with a three-stage contrastive framework over language-audio, track-track, and track-playlist relationships.
The authors report superior efficacy on two public datasets and release code and dataset resources.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework applies progressively task-specific contrastive objectives across within-track, track, and playlist relationships.

interpretation.claim: Cold-start recommendation may benefit from learning relational representations at multiple abstraction levels rather than relying only on item-content representations.

application.claim: For another cold-start multimodal recommendation task, consider staged objectives that align modalities within items and then model item-to-item and item-to-context relationships.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this staged strategy will transfer to other domains, datasets, or recommendation settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the two datasets.
Quantitative results, evaluation metrics, and statistical comparisons are not provided.
Model architecture details, training settings, and ablation results are not provided.
The scope and terms of the code and dataset release are not specified.
